Thanks again for the call today - really useful to see Acme.ai's production profile. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before I circulate a short proposal: 

Summary of requirements (per call)
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency target ~150ms for text-gen endpoint (50-256 tokens typical).
- Peak concurrency: ~700-900 concurrent active requests at peak (global), ~2.5M tokens/min sustained at heavy times.
- Streaming: yes, streaming partial tokens is required for the user experience (client does incremental rendering).
- Connection model: multiple clients will open persistent connections from edge servers (pooling expected; each edge pool ~200 connections).

Open items / asks for you
1) Confirm peak concurrency window (are 700-900 estimates peak per region or global?)
2) Share sample request size distribution (typical tokens in / out) - helps with batching and kernel selection.
3) Any hard constraints on token-rate vs. connection QPS?

What I'll send next (by EOD Tuesday):
- Redwood recommended rate-limit profile + optional Dedicated capacity quote (attachment stub).
- Suggested connection-pooling guidance (keep-alive, max connections per client) and a short ramp plan to reach 1k concurrency safely.

If that looks right I'll loop in Vivek for the Dedicated capacity pricing and Laura for the security on streaming.

Thanks,

Appreciate the details, Alex - that helps. Attached is a short proposal (redwood_rate_limit_proposal.pdf) that shows two profiles: Hosted API with soft rate limits + Dedicated capacity with hard quotas. Highlights: 

Recommended default profile (Hosted):
- Per-client QPS: 200 QPS per origin by default; additional bursts handled via short token-bucket (burst 2x for 30s).
- Token-rate throttles: soft throttle at 300k tokens/min per API key, hard throttle at 600k tokens/min.
- Streaming: we surface chunked streaming with an idle keep-alive of 60s; recommended client-side connection pooling of 50-200 conns per edge pool.

Dedicated option (for predictable tail latency):
- Reserved concurrency units (RCUs) that map to sustained concurrent generation slots. We can size to 1,000 RCUs to cover your 700-900 peak.
- Guaranteed p95 latency targets (SLA path) for reserved capacity; fallback to hosted model variants if capacity disrupted.

Operational notes:
- For your mix (short requests + occasional 500-token jobs) we recommend a hybrid: reserve core RCUs to serve tail latency, keep hosted for burst overflow.
- Connection pooling: set keep-alive and use long-lived connections; aim for max 150 connections per edge instance and use a client-side leaky-bucket for QPS smoothing.

I've looped in Vivek to call out pricing models and Laura for any security/streaming compliance notes. Next step: technical call to finalize per-region quotas and a short pilot plan.

Attachments: redwood_rate_limit_proposal.pdf (pricing + rate profiles)

- Marissa
